text: Both consulting and in-house ServiceNow work are real, common, respected career paths. Neither is a stepping stone to the other, and neither is the serious path while the other is a fallback. They're structurally different jobs that happen to use the same platform skills — the right one depends on what you actually want your week, and your next few years, to look like.

At an implementation partner firm, you're typically staffed on client engagements with a defined scope and timeline, moving between client environments relatively often, sometimes with real travel depending on the firm. The upside is concrete: you get exposure to a wider variety of instances, industries, and architecture decisions in a shorter span of time, because each new engagement often means a different CMDB structure, a different integration landscape, a different set of governance constraints. The tradeoff is real too — less day-to-day stability, project-based pressure, and a travel expectation that doesn't fit every life circumstance.

An in-house role means working for one employer on that employer's own instance. The upside is depth — living with the long-term consequences of architecture and configuration decisions, including ones made before you joined, and building deep understanding of one complex environment over years. Day-to-day predictability is usually higher, with no client travel and a clearer sense of how your work fits one organization's roadmap. The tradeoff is the mirror image: your exposure to different architecture patterns and industries is naturally narrower.

Neither path wins the CTA-readiness question outright. Consulting can deliver broad exposure faster; a long in-house tenure at a large, complex enterprise with real architecture responsibility can build comparably deep readiness within one environment. What actually matters is whether your day-to-day work includes real architectural decision-making, not which structural category your employer falls into. When evaluating an offer, ask about the actual substance of the work, and weigh your own travel tolerance and appetite for variety versus depth honestly.
That closes this chapter on the real ServiceNow job market. Next, Chapter 3 turns to building a portfolio — starting with what to showcase from this path's own projects.
